title: Review: National and global energy resources; Current, potential difference and resistance
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank for AQA GCSE Physics (8463) (review status in the bank: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms: 4.1.3-c06, 4.1.3-c11, 4.2.1-c13, 4.2.1-c07. Questions: 4.1.3-q13, 4.1.3-q14, 4.1.3-q15, 4.1.3-q16, 4.1.3-q03, 4.2.1-q01, 4.2.1-q03, 4.1.3-q12, 4.2.1-q02, 4.2.1-q06, 4.1.3-q04, 4.2.1-q04. assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Hydro-electricity
items.clue: Uses water stored behind a dam.

items.label: Renewable energy resource
items.clue: One that is replenished as it is used.

items.label: Ohm (Ω)
items.clue: The unit equal to one volt per ampere.

items.label: Ampere (A)
items.clue: The unit for the rate of flow of charge.

questions.stem: Which environmental impact arises directly from burning fossil fuels in a power station?

options.text: Carbon dioxide and sulfur dioxide are released into the air
Radioactive waste is produced and has to be stored safely
The steam from the cooling towers poisons nearby land
Acid rain is formed by the carbon dioxide given off

questions.explanation: Burning releases carbon dioxide, which contributes to global warming, and sulfur dioxide, which causes acid rain.

questions.stem: Which statement about the environmental impact of renewable energy resources is correct?

options.text: They cause no environmental damage of any kind at all
They have impacts too, such as land flooded behind a hydro dam
Bio-fuel is the one renewable that has no effect at all on land use
Their only impact is the carbon dioxide released in use

questions.explanation: Renewable does not mean harmless: dams flood valleys, wind farms alter landscapes and habitats, fuel crops use land.

questions.stem: The share of UK electricity generated from renewable resources has risen sharply since 2010. Which explanation of this trend is best?

options.text: The UK's coal, oil and gas have now all been used up
Renewables can now supply power at all times without any backup
Concern about carbon dioxide, and cheaper wind and solar
Fossil fuels have been replaced completely across all energy use

questions.explanation: Environmental concern plus falling cost is what has driven the change, supported by government policy.

questions.stem: Scientists identified the harm caused by burning fossil fuels many years ago, yet their use has continued. Which statement best explains this?

options.text: The evidence is still too uncertain for anyone to act on it
Scientists have not yet explained the harm to any government
No other energy resource could possibly replace the fossil fuels
Political, social, ethical and economic factors count too

questions.explanation: Science can identify an environmental issue but does not always have the power to deal with it; cost, jobs, public opinion and government policy all bear on what is done.

questions.stem: Which statement is the specification's definition of a renewable energy resource?

options.text: One with a supply so large that it could never all be used up
One that gives off no carbon dioxide while it is being used
One that is being, or can be, replenished as it is used
One that costs nothing to use once it has been built

questions.explanation: This is the definition word for word: replacement keeping pace with use.

questions.stem: A circuit diagram shows a component drawn as a plain rectangle with an arrow across it at an angle. Which component is it?

options.text: a variable resistor, whose resistance is set by hand by moving a slider
an LDR, whose resistance falls when the light shining on it brightens
a thermistor, whose resistance changes when its temperature alters
a diode, which allows a current through it in one direction only

questions.explanation: The standard symbol for a variable resistor is the resistor rectangle with an arrow drawn diagonally across it, showing a resistance that can be adjusted.

questions.stem: A closed loop of copper wire contains no cell and no power supply. Why is there no current in it?

options.text: the free electrons in the copper drift round on their own, making a current
a complete copper loop needs no cell, so a current flows round it
there is no source of potential difference to make the charge flow
copper has a resistance far too low for a current to be set up

questions.explanation: The specification is explicit: for charge to flow through a closed circuit the circuit must include a source of potential difference.

questions.stem: Tidal energy is described as a reliable energy resource. Which statement explains why?

options.text: The tides are driven by winds that blow daily
Tidal stations give out more energy than any other
The sea is pushed along by winds that never stop
The tides rise and fall on a known cycle

questions.explanation: The times of high and low water are set by the Moon and the Sun and can be predicted years ahead.

questions.stem: A student is drawing a circuit diagram to measure the current through a lamp and the potential difference across it. Where should the two meters be drawn?

options.text: the voltmeter in the loop with the lamp, and the ammeter across it
the ammeter in the loop with the lamp and the voltmeter across it
both meters drawn in the loop, one on each side of the lamp
both meters drawn across the lamp, in parallel with each other

questions.explanation: The charge to be counted must pass through the ammeter, so it goes in series; the voltmeter compares the potential at the lamp's two ends, so it goes across it.

questions.stem: In the equation Q = I t, which set of units is correct for the three quantities?

options.text: charge flow in amperes, current in coulombs, and time in seconds
charge flow in coulombs, current in amperes, time in seconds
charge flow in coulombs, current in amperes and time in minutes
charge flow in coulombs, current in coulombs, time in seconds

questions.explanation: Exactly as the specification gives them: charge flow, Q, in coulombs, C; current, I, in amperes, A; time, t, in seconds, s.

questions.stem: Nuclear fuel is classified as non-renewable. Which reason for that classification is correct?

options.text: Uranium is mined from rock, so it is a fossil fuel
Nuclear power stations release carbon dioxide as they run
The clouds from its cooling towers add carbon dioxide
The uranium used is not replenished as it is used

questions.explanation: Applies the definition directly: the fuel in the ground is not being replaced as it is consumed.

questions.stem: What is meant by the size of the electric current in a wire?

options.text: the total charge that has flowed since the circuit was switched on
the speed at which the individual electrons drift along the wire
the energy that the cell transfers to the wire in each second
the rate of flow of electrical charge past a given point in the wire

questions.explanation: The specification defines the size of the electric current as the rate of flow of electrical charge, that is, the charge passing a point each second.
